title: How to add speaker notes in PowerPoint on Mac: step by step for Microsoft 365

description: Learn how to add speaker notes in PowerPoint on Mac, then use Presenter View and print them. Clear menu paths and shortcuts for Microsoft 365.

intro: Switch to View > Normal, select a slide, click the “Click to add notes” box under it, and type. Your notes appear in Presenter View when you start the show with View > Presenter View or ⌥ Return, and the audience sees only the slides.
tldr: Choose View > Normal (⌘1), select a slide, and click “Click to add notes” under it.
Hide or show the notes area with the Notes button in the bottom bar. I found no verified shortcut for it.

Print notes with File > Print, then choose Notes Pages under Print Layout.
If notes are cut off in Presenter View, drag that window left until the notes pane shows.

blocks.text: Speaker notes are private text you attach to each slide. They help you remember the point, the example, or the number you want to say next. The audience never sees them on the screen. That makes them a good place for detail that would clutter a slide.
What speaker notes do and where they appear

Notes live with each slide in the presentation file. When you present in Presenter View, you see the current slide, a preview of the next slide, and that slide's notes. The audience sees only the slides. That split is the whole point. You can glance at a short cue while the room looks at a clean chart. Notes can also be printed, which is handy for a rehearsal copy.
Check your PowerPoint version first

Microsoft's speaker notes article covers PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint 2024, and PowerPoint 2021, each including Mac. It also lists PowerPoint 2019 and PowerPoint 2016. If you use any of those on a Mac, the basic steps are the same. To check your version, open the PowerPoint menu and look for About PowerPoint. Microsoft's About Office example uses Word, so the PowerPoint menu should match, but I did not confirm that in PowerPoint itself. The most recent Mac build in Microsoft's release notes is 16.114.3, dated October 27, 2026.

blocks.title: Screenshots are from 2016
blocks.text: Microsoft's Mac steps were captured with PowerPoint 2016 for Mac screenshots. Microsoft 365 may place the Notes button or a menu item in a slightly different spot. If a name does not match, search the Help menu for the same word.
Add speaker notes in Normal view

Normal view is where you write notes. The slide sits in the middle, the thumbnails run down the left, and the notes area sits under the slide. If you are in another view, choose View > Normal first. Then click a thumbnail. The slide and its notes area change together, so each note belongs to the slide you selected.

Click the box that says “Click to add notes”, then type. A cursor appears inside the box once it is active. Keep your first notes short. A cue such as “Pause, ask about churn” is easier to use than a paragraph you have to read. You glance at notes while you talk, so short beats long.
Hide the notes pane without losing your notes

The Notes button in the bottom bar of the window hides and shows the notes pane. Microsoft describes this as hiding the pane, which is a display setting. Show the pane again and check a slide to be sure its notes are still there. I did not find a verified keyboard shortcut for the Notes pane, so use the button.
Review notes in Notes Page view

Notes Page view shows each slide with its notes below it, one slide per page. Press ⌘3 or choose View > Notes Page. Read through the pages to catch typos and confirm every slide has the note you meant. Press ⌘1 to return to Normal view. Indezine's shortcut list was last updated July 29, 2021, so confirm the keys in your build.
Present with notes in Presenter View

Choose View > Presenter View, or press ⌥ Return, to start the show with Presenter View. The presenter screen shows the current slide, a preview of the next slide, and the notes for the current slide. Microsoft's page does not say whether Presenter View is on by default on Mac, so test it before a live talk. Some guides place this command under Slide Show instead, so check there if View does not show it.
Keyboard shortcuts that help while you present

These shortcuts come from Microsoft's shortcut article and from Indezine's list for PowerPoint 365 for Mac. Microsoft warns that some shortcuts conflict with macOS settings or utility apps. Test each one before you rely on it during a talk.

items: Use ⌥ Return when you want the notes on your screen and the slides on the audience's screen.
Use ⌘Return when you are mid-deck and want to start from the slide you are on.
Use ⌘⇧Return when you want to rehearse from the first slide.
Use ⌘. or Esc when you finish and want to stop the show.

blocks.text: In Presenter View on Mac, Control+Tab moves focus into the Notes pane. Plain Tab inserts a tab character there instead. Keyboard navigation in Presenter View needs macOS 10.15 Catalina or later and the keyboard navigation setting. Without VoiceOver, you turn that setting on in the keyboard shortcut settings. Older macOS versions call this System Preferences. Newer versions call it System Settings, so the path may differ on your Mac.
Fix notes that don't show in Presenter View

The most common problem is a Presenter View window that sits partly off the screen. The notes pane gets cut off, and it looks as if the notes are gone. Drag the window left to bring the notes into view. A Microsoft Q&A thread from October 2021 describes this fix for PowerPoint 16.54 on Mac. It drew more than 100 “same question” follow-ups, and its accepted answer has more than 30 helpful votes. The fix still applies, but the thread is old, so check your build if the window will not move.
Print speaker notes from a Mac

Choose File > Print. Pick your printer under Printer. Under Settings, open the dropdown next to Full Page Slides, choose Notes Pages under Print Layout, and click Print. Only one slide and its notes appear on each printed page. Microsoft's print article has no Mac-specific steps and uses Windows-style dialog names, so some labels may differ on your screen. Check the page preview before you commit paper to the job.
Print notes without slide thumbnails

Some presenters want the notes without the small slide picture. Choose View > Notes Page. Select the slide thumbnail on each notes page and press Delete. This removes the picture from the printout only. The slide stays in the presentation. Go through every notes page before you print, because each thumbnail needs its own removal.
Make a notes handout when Create Handouts is missing

Microsoft's Windows-style article describes File > Export > Create Handouts, which sends slides and notes to Word. A Microsoft Q&A answer from December 2025 says Create Handouts is not available on macOS. The workaround in that thread is File > Print, Notes in the Layout menu, Save as PDF from the PDF menu, then opening the PDF in Word. That answer came from a community member, not Microsoft staff. The original poster said it worked, so test it on a short deck first.
Speaker notes in PowerPoint for the web

PowerPoint for the web can write notes. Use the View tab, then Show, then Notes. You can resize the pane by dragging its top border. The web version cannot show notes during a slide show, so present from a desktop app such as PowerPoint for Mac. Printing notes from the web works only for Microsoft 365 business subscribers whose file sits on OneDrive for work or school or SharePoint.
Mistakes that make notes less useful
Most note problems come from how the notes are written, not from the menus. These habits cause the most trouble on stage.

items: Writing a full script, then reading it word for word. The room notices, and the notes stop being cues.
Putting your notes on the slide. Notes are for you, and the audience sees the slide.
Leaving the key slides blank, so you improvise the point you care about most.
Presenting without a Presenter View check. Start the show once before the talk.
Printing without checking Notes Page view first. Layout problems show up on paper.

blocks.text: Reading slides to the audience was the top annoyance in a 2019 survey by Dave Paradi, which had 236 respondents. Notes help you avoid that habit. Write cues, not sentences that copy the slide. The survey did not measure how many presenters use speaker notes, so read it as a sign of audience habits, not notes use.
What to do next

Run one slide through the full path before a live talk. Add a note, switch to Notes Page view, start Presenter View, and check that the notes pane is on screen. Then print or save a PDF copy if you need one. If a menu name differs from this guide, check your version number first. Then search the Help menu for the exact wording on your screen.

faq.question: Where do speaker notes appear when I present on a Mac?
faq.answer: They appear in Presenter View, not on the slide the audience sees. Start it with View > Presenter View or ⌥ Return. The presenter screen shows the current slide, a preview of the next slide, and that slide's notes.

faq.question: Can I add speaker notes in PowerPoint for the web?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the View tab, then Show, then Notes. The web version cannot show notes during a slide show, so present from a desktop app such as PowerPoint for Mac.

faq.question: Why are my notes missing in Presenter View?
faq.answer: The most common cause is a Presenter View window that sits partly off the screen. Drag it left to reveal the notes pane. If the notes are truly empty, check in Normal view that you typed them on that slide.

faq.question: Can I print speaker notes from PowerPoint on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose File > Print, open the dropdown next to Full Page Slides, then choose Notes Pages under Print Layout. Each printed page holds one slide and its notes.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to hide the Notes pane?
faq.answer: I did not find a verified shortcut for it. Use the Notes button in the bottom bar of the window. Indezine's shortcut list has no entry for the pane, so the button is the safe route.

faq.question: Which versions of PowerPoint does this guide cover?
faq.answer: Microsoft's speaker notes article covers PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, 2024, and 2021, each including Mac. It also lists PowerPoint 2019 and 2016. The Mac screenshots come from 2016, so menu names may shift in newer builds.

faq.question: Can I turn my notes into a Word handout on a Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Create Handouts option is not available on macOS, according to a Microsoft Q&A answer from December 2025. A community workaround is to print to PDF with the Notes layout, then open the PDF in Word.

task: Add speaker notes to a slide in PowerPoint on Mac
requirements: PowerPoint for Mac from Microsoft 365, 2024, 2021, 2019, or 2016
A presentation open in PowerPoint with at least one slide
macOS 10.15 Catalina or later if you want Presenter View keyboard navigation

steps.name: Open the presentation in Normal view
steps.text: Open your file in PowerPoint for Mac. Choose View > Normal, or press ⌘1. Normal view shows the thumbnails on the left, the slide in the middle, and the notes area under the slide.

steps.name: Select the slide you want to annotate
steps.text: Click the slide thumbnail in the left pane. The large slide changes to match. Any note you type now attaches to that slide and no other.
steps.tip: Scroll the thumbnails to find the slide you need before you click.

steps.name: Click the notes box
steps.text: Find the box under the slide that says Click to add notes. Click inside it. A cursor appears, and the box is ready for text.

steps.name: Type your note
steps.text: Write the cue you need while you talk. Use a short phrase, a number, or the example you want to tell. Keep it short enough to scan in one glance.

steps.name: Repeat for each slide
steps.text: Click the next thumbnail and repeat the steps. A slide with no notes shows an empty box, so scroll the thumbnails and check each one before you present.

steps.name: Hide or show the notes pane
steps.text: Click the Notes button in the bottom bar to hide the pane. Click it again to show the pane. Microsoft's steps describe this button, and I did not find a keyboard shortcut for it.
steps.tip: Hiding the pane changes the view. Show it again to check your notes.

steps.name: Check your notes in Notes Page view
steps.text: Choose View > Notes Page, or press ⌘3. Each page shows a slide with its notes, so you can read the whole talk in order. Press ⌘1 to return to Normal view.

steps.name: Start Presenter View
steps.text: Choose View > Presenter View, or press ⌥ Return. The presenter screen shows the current slide, a preview of the next slide, and your notes. The audience sees only the slides.
steps.tip: If you do not see Presenter View under View, check the Slide Show menu. Some guides list it there.

steps.name: Bring cut-off notes back into view
steps.text: If the notes pane is cut off, drag the Presenter View window to the left until the notes show. This is the fix that Microsoft's Q&A thread describes for a notes pane that seems to be missing.
steps.tip: Drag the window by its frame, not the slide inside it.

steps.name: Print your speaker notes
steps.text: Choose File > Print. Pick your printer under Printer. Open the dropdown next to Full Page Slides under Settings, choose Notes Pages under Print Layout, then click Print. Each printed page holds one slide and its notes.
steps.tip: Microsoft's print article uses Windows-style names. Look for the same words if a label differs.

steps.name: Print notes without slide thumbnails
steps.text: Choose View > Notes Page. Select the slide thumbnail on each notes page and press Delete. The picture leaves the printout only, and the slide stays in your presentation. Then print as usual.
steps.tip: Save a copy of the file first, so you can get the thumbnails back if you need them.

steps.name: Save notes as a PDF to open in Word
steps.text: Choose File > Print. Pick Notes in the Layout menu, then choose Save as PDF from the PDF menu. Open the saved PDF in Word. This route comes from a community answer, not Microsoft documentation.
steps.tip: The original poster reported that it worked. Try it on a short deck first.

troubleshooting.problem: The Click to add notes box is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Choose View > Normal, then click the Notes button in the bottom bar. If the box is still hidden, click the slide thumbnail and check the pane again.

troubleshooting.problem: Notes don't show in Presenter View
troubleshooting.fix: Drag the Presenter View window left so the notes pane is on screen. Microsoft's Q&A thread from October 2021 describes the same fix for PowerPoint 16.54.

troubleshooting.problem: A keyboard shortcut does nothing on Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Some shortcuts conflict with macOS settings or utility apps. Check your keyboard settings, or quit the utility app that uses the same keys, then try again.

troubleshooting.problem: Create Handouts is missing from the File menu
troubleshooting.fix: Create Handouts is not available on macOS, according to a December 2025 Microsoft Q&A answer. Print to PDF with the Notes layout, then open the PDF in Word.

troubleshooting.problem: Control+Tab does not move focus to the notes
troubleshooting.fix: Presenter View keyboard navigation needs macOS 10.15 Catalina or later and the keyboard navigation setting. Without VoiceOver, turn that setting on in your keyboard shortcut settings.

troubleshooting.problem: Notes do not show during a slide show in PowerPoint for the web
troubleshooting.fix: Microsoft says you need a desktop version of PowerPoint to see notes while presenting. Open the file in PowerPoint for Mac and start Presenter View from there.
